_readme: THE PAIR TABLE — what taste.py asks, in order, and the exact state behind each side.
Data, not code, and hardcoded rather than read from the presets, at K.'s call:
'I like to have a paper trail considering the llm usage here.' A preset can be
edited later and would silently rewrite what an old log entry meant; these numbers
cannot. A pair here plus a line in docs/TASTE-LOG.md reconstructs any answer,
Ranked by Fable (the VP): unblocks-the-most x cheap-to-ask x needs-real-lamps.
Items 1-5 are one sitting (~20-30 min). 6-8 are night two; the resume pointer is
kind: 'pair'     -> two sides, A vs B, the normal case.
kind: 'keepcut'  -> one thing at a time, keep or cut. Used where a pair would be
FALSE PRECISION: an A-vs-B tap between exhibit #14 and #22 says
nothing about a pool of 38. Fable's call, and it is right.
cost:            -> printed BEFORE the side plays. A B-side that costs 3-6x compute
gets rejected for lag, not for looks, unless the cost is named
first. That contamination is the failure mode this field exists
scope:           -> SCREEN or LAMPS or ROOM. Printed before anything moves, so the
right surface is being watched when it does.

_why: K.: 'you will be in complete control. so figure out a default value.'
So every session starts from ONE known state and every pair is a departure from
it, not from wherever last night's experiment left the room. Factory config,
attract mode off (the room must not wander mid-question), overlap off, zoom on
the pendulum, business pinned at 0.45 -- high enough that the pendulum swings and
the dive actually dives, low enough that it is not a carnival. Restored on exit.

pairs.question: Which dive is right?
pairs.watch: the middle of the frame as it pulls in and lets go
pairs.unblocks: whether the whole 21 zoom-lens rework stands as shipped, or gets revisited

sides.label: A
sides.name: lens (magnify the middle, frame edge stays put)

sides.label: B
sides.name: uniform (the whole frame scales -- the original)

pairs.question: Does the colour change read as drift, or as mud?
pairs.watch: the lamps as the scene changes -- the screen is not the question here
pairs.note: The C# layer's own colorDrift is pinned at 0.02 in party-main.js and is NOT what moves between these sides. Only the scene fade does. If it muds on BOTH sides, that is the two-motions bug and it needs the Hue repo, not this slider.
pairs.unblocks: paletteFade default, and whether the two-colour-motions bug is real

sides.label: B
sides.name: 20 s fade (slow enough to be unmistakably drift)

pairs.question: How many colours should be left as it resolves?
pairs.watch: the colours as the pattern settles into symmetry
pairs.unblocks: colorSpreadOrder default -- I changed this from 0.34 to 0.55 today on inference alone

sides.label: A
sides.name: rich (0.55 -- today's new default, several roles survive the resolve)

sides.label: B
sides.name: converging (0.2 -- close to how it behaved before today)

pairs.question: Newton is soft now, not sharp. Keep it, or is the haze worse than the blocks?
pairs.watch: the three basins where they meet -- detail vs mush
pairs.cost: There is no B side to show you. Sharp is not a setting -- it is 3-6x the compute on all three escape-time exhibits, and Mandelbrot already lagged. This asks whether that work is worth queueing, so answer the picture, not the price.
pairs.unblocks: whether to queue the sharp-render job at all

pairs.question: Two exhibits in one frame -- fading out behind, or staying?
pairs.watch: what happens to the previous shape when the new one arrives
pairs.cost: B (persistent) roughly DOUBLES render cost. If it stutters, that is the price showing, not the look -- say so and I will log it as a cost rejection rather than a taste one.
pairs.unblocks: overlapMode default, and whether the expensive exhibits need vetoing from layering

sides.label: A
sides.name: transition (the old shape fades away behind the new one)

sides.label: B
sides.name: persistent (it stays underneath for the whole dwell)

pairs.question: Keep this one in the room, or cut it?
pairs.watch: whether it performs, and whether it cuts instead of dissolving
pairs.note: Capped at the flagged-risky ones rather than touring all 38. Mandelbrot lagged; the opaque ones repaint the whole frame and can only ever be the bottom overlap layer, which may break the flow-into-each-other feel even when they run fine.
pairs.unblocks: the veto list -- which exhibits the room never shows

pairs.question: Is this bloom worth keeping as a starting point?
pairs.watch: the centre, the four streams, and whether the corners ever light
pairs.note: Each of these sets all 19 bloom knobs at once. The question is not which is prettiest -- it is which are worth landing on before tuning by hand.
pairs.unblocks: which of the 8 snap points survive

items.name: four corners -- the arrival is the event
hard edges -- dark between the pulses
flood -- everything at the top of its range

pairs.question: Does this colour mode earn its place?
pairs.note: Cutting three would make the catalog better than adding an eighth. Ember is the one to watch -- its flare may be too rare to ever notice.
pairs.unblocks: which of the seven cards stay in the catalog

items.name: Runner (a band moving outward, not a lamp-by-lamp chase)

_not_asked_here: 8.0 Q9 (31 sliders -- collapse the chaos/order pairs into one knob?) and Q10 (which
LFO patches are worth keeping) are deliberately absent. Both need K. operating the
dashboard directly, not watching a driven pair. Fable's call; flagged rather than
The accent now appearing in the ambient ramp (STATE 2026-07-25) is also absent: there
is no runtime flag to turn it back off, so there is no B side to show. It needs a
code change to ask properly, and it is worth asking properly -- it reverses a call
8.0 Q3 (attract dwell 25-45 s) is absent because dwell is randomised per cycle and
not a config key. Auditioning it means the dashboard's skip button, not a pair.
